newsitem.title: USA: Conrail reiterates desire to merge with CSX.
newsitem.headline: Conrail reiterates desire to merge with CSX.

text.p: Conrail Inc. Wednesday reiterated its desire to merge with CSX Corp. after CSX slightly sweetened the cash portion of its $8.4 billion bid for the eastern railroad, which is also being pursued by Norfolk Southern Corp.
Conrail said its board had considered the merits of the rival bids and reaffirmed that a merger with CSX was a superior strategic combination.
The merging of CSX and Conrail would create one of the largest transportation companies in the world, including a rail system with some 29,000 miles (47,000 km) of routes in 22 eastern states.
Norfolk Southern, meanwhile, issued a terse statement reaffirming its $100-a-share all-cash offer, which amounts to about $9.1 billion. It also said it had terminated its discussions with Conrail.
CSX said in a joint statement with Conrail that it raised the cash portion of its offer to $110 for each Conrail share, which would value the entire transaction at $8.383 billion.

Under the revised CSX offer, the Richmond, Va.-based railroad will pay $4.01 billion for 40 percent of Conrail's 91 million outstanding shares and offer 1.85619 of a CSX share, or about $4.38 billion based on Wednesday's trading price of $43.25, for the remaining shares.

That would value Philadelphia-based Conrail's shares at about $93 each, far less than the $100 in cash that Norfolk Southern is offering. Conrail's stock gained $1.375 to $93.625 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

"It is clear to me that CSX and Conrail intend to continue their joint efforts to railroad Conrail shareholders into accepting a proposal significantly inferior to Norfolk Southern's $100 per share all cash tender offer," Norfolk Southern Charman David R. Goode said in a statement.

"Until CSX acknowledges that all Conrail shareholders are entitled to the $100 cash that they can only receive from Norfolk Southern's offer, any discussions between us are a waste of time," Goode added.

CSX Chairman John Snow said in the statement that the company's decision to raise its cash offer followed an analysis that identified at least $730 million in synergies and cost savings in a CSX-Conrail combination -- $180 million more than originally anticipated.
"Clearly, the combination of CSX and Conrail provides the best overall package of benefits to our constituencies, including customers, the communities we serve, and the public-at-large," Snow said.
"We welcome the strong support of the Conrail board of directors and look forward to a bright future as our new company moves full speed into the 21st century."
Snow also said that the Norfolk Southern bid was burdened with a number of conditions that would force Conrail shareholders to wait a prolonged amount of time to receive payment for their shares.
Norfolk Southern disputed that contention, however, saying that its offer included setting up a trust that would provide immediate cash payment to all shareholders.
The CSX-Conrail announcement also said that a Conrail shareholders' meeting scheduled for Nov. 14 had been cancelled, with a new meeting meeting expected to be held in mid-December.
It also said that the period during which the Conrail board cannot withdraw its support for the merger or agree to any competing deals will be extended to July 12.
Under the amended terms, CSX's tender offer's expiration date and withdrawal and proration rights were extended until midnight Nov. 20.
